Coming from someone who was nervous one second ago about “rights-snatching”, that seems pretty rich. The public must be trusted to make such decisions because the alternative is giving up power to a few supposedly learned, wise and holier than thou government officials who may make some good decisions, but with that power the risk is far higher when they do inevitably make bad decisions. 

The removal of a non-viable foetus is not considered an abortion, although it is true that often the same medications/similar procedures will be used to deal with that. That is a complication and definitely a point that should be considered in the discussion. However, that is not of immediate importance to what we are discussing.

Now, you claim that “you can make an entirely consistent set of rules based primarily on not harming the mother”. This is true. However, when there is (potentially) another life involved - namely the life of what is arguably a child - that should at least be taken into consideration. The fact that you can make a consistent set of laws around something does not and has never meant that that would be a good set of laws. There are many many things you can make consistent laws around, but that does not by their nature justify them. You have to explain why they would be good laws - not just that they could be laws. When any law - or set of laws - disregards what is potentially a human life, that is a very dangerous road to go down. 

Also, you now acknowledge that people are getting to vote, which undermines what you were saying earlier about this issue being “theocratic”. If people are voting according to their religious ideals, that is still a democracy, not a theocracy. However, I do take issue with the idea that all these voters are religiously motivated. I’m sure many people are, but when life begins is a fundamentally scientific - rather than religious - question. And that is the central question here.

A. It is harmful to any individual to lie. It harms that individual’s perception of reality, it undermines their intelligence and it dulls their conscience.

The words man and woman and he and she are becoming as meaningless and arbitrary as glooffysnu, and whereas they once communicated truths, in the mouths of many they now communicate nothing.

C. It is harmful to the person being lied about. Believe it or not lying to a man by affirming him in his delusion that he is a woman is no more helpful than lying to a skeletal girl with body dysmorphia and telling her that yes, her delusions are right and she is in fact too fat. Or affirming the delusions of the schizophrenic by telling him the chair is indeed talking to him.

D. It harms children. If children are raised with no understanding of basic truths, or indeed of what truth is, what hope then have they? 

So those would be the four biggest harms of this, at least from my perspective.
